title: The HBO series Treme
summary: Player praises the show's authenticity, and Rowe tells of a realistic amp detail.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Do you think the HBO series “Treme” has done a good job with trying to capture that?

I think they’ve done an excellent job in trying to capture it. It’s the closest thing — and it’s funny because I wasn’t born in New Orleans, it’s interesting when I talk to a lot of my colleagues who, maybe who are New Orleanians, they’re very, very protective in ways, of their culture. So when you see something like the HBO “Treme” series, you know I’ve heard different ones comment like, oh you know, that club — they’re like, when they look at it they’re so meticulous, like oh this club wouldn’t have these chairs there. You know what I mean? Or this wouldn’t be this way. And there have been other shows in the past, series or movie series, or whatever, that have tried to portray New Orleans and they, in my opinion, were terrible. I mean there’s nothing like New Orleans. It’s like that doesn’t even make sense, like the way they move from a shot to some other shot, and they have no continuity. You know, it’s like that’s completely Uptown, and this place is — it just doesn’t make sense what they just did. But the “Treme” series I think is — I mean when I watch it it’s like yeah, this is the real thing. But some people I find, that some people from New Orleans are even more particular about, do they have every single thing exactly like — I mean it’s Hollywood. So that what I think is a disconnect. But I think that “Treme” has done an excellent job. And I think that it’s brought a lot of great © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-
notoriety to the world, Then people can go maybe — it will inspire people to go and check out New Orleans, that maybe never would have before.

I remember seeing a rehearsal scene, and some guitar player got angry or something, and he yanked his thing out of his amp. And someone was smart enough to know, if you yank your — if the amp is on, it’s going to make a sound. And it did. And I said, “now see, a lot of times no one would think of that.”

Exactly. Yeah. And that’s exactly what I mean by, that these people were very, I think, excellent in the recreation of what it would be like in New Orleans. And yeah. So I think they’ve done a great job.
